title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the notes on the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, Grothendieck wants to rebuild the homotopy types of open strata, and of unions of strata, of a normal-crossings compactification from 'elementary' local types. These elementary types are punctured tubular neighbourhoods V^{d'}_{d,d''} of one stratum relative to others. He tests the idea on the local model X = C^2 with divisor Δ1 ∪ Δ2 (the two coordinate axes) and P = origin. The previous page listed the 'global' opens: X, U1 = C^2∖Δ1, U2 = C^2∖Δ2, U = U1 ∪ U2 = C^2∖{P}, and U1 ∩ U2 = C*×C*. It also recorded the decomposition C = C* ⊔_{D*} D.

(280) U = C^2∖{P} is written as an amalgamated sum (homotopy colimit) of the zigzag C*×D ← C*×D* → C*×C* ← D*×C* → D×C*. This comes from writing U2 = C*×C as C*×C* ∪_{C*×D*} C*×D, writing U1 = C×C* as C*×C* ∪_{D*×C*} D×C*, and then gluing U1 and U2 along C*×C*. In homotopy terms the zigzag is S^1 ← T^2 → T^2 ← T^2 → S^1. It collapses to the join S^1 * S^1 = S^3, which is indeed the homotopy type of C^2∖{0}.

(281) C×C is written as the amalgamated sum of the 3×3 diagram. This diagram is the product of the span-shaped category (· ← · → ·) with itself, applied to the span C* ← D* → D in each factor. Its entries, read as rows in the second factor and columns in the first, are:
- C*×C*, D*×C*, D×C*
- C*×D*, D*×D*, D×D*
- C*×D, D*×D, D×D
The colimit is (C* ⊔_{D*} D)^2 = C^2, which is contractible. Two entries are labelled as the new elementary types:
- D×D* = V^{Δ2}_{P,x}: the neighbourhood of P with one branch removed.
- D*×D = V^{Δ1}_{P,x}: the neighbourhood with the other branch removed.
The centre D*×D* is the fully punctured 'D_0^*' of the previous page.

The next page confirms the purpose. These diagrams show how the types V^{Δi}_{P,x} enter. He then intends to study the variance of V^{d'_0}_{d_*,d''_0} under change of strata, and of the associated Π1 (fundamental groupoids), so as to reconstruct all 'modular types' and the fundamental groupoids of the stratification.
errors: No mathematical error. Both amalgamated sums are correct as covers by opens or tubular models, hence as homotopy pushouts.

Minor notational ambiguity: which of D×D* and D*×D is called V^{Δ1} versus V^{Δ2} depends on an unstated convention for which axis is Δ1. The page is internally consistent with D×D* (removing the second-coordinate axis) labelled Δ2.
The vertical arrows in (281) point up from the middle row and down from the middle row. This correctly reflects the span shape C* ← D* → D in the second factor.

ideas.what: Homotopy type of C^2∖{0} as an iterated homotopy pushout of products of C*, D*, D (a 5-term zigzag), i.e. the join S^1*S^1 = S^3
ideas.modern_name: homotopy pushout / Mayer–Vietoris gluing; boundary of the real oriented blow-up (plumbing) of a normal crossing point
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (plumbing descriptions: Mumford 1961, Hirzebruch; join decompositions are standard)

ideas.what: C×C as the colimit of the product of the span C* ← D* → D with itself: a cubical (3×3) diagram indexed by pairs of strata, whose entries are punctured polydisc neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: decomposition of a normal-crossings stratified space by homotopy links / exit-path data (product of local spans); Kato–Nakayama / real-blow-up toric pieces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (homotopy links, 1988), MacPherson–Treumann–Lurie (exit-path categories), Kato–Nakayama (1999) for the log-geometric version
ideas.where_published: The programme of reconstructing a stratified space from strata and tubular neighbourhoods is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'tame topology'; this explicit example is not there.

ideas.what: Elementary types V^{d'}_{d,d''} (tubular neighbourhood of a stratum with some divisor branches removed) as the building blocks from which global 'modular types' and their fundamental groupoids are glued
ideas.modern_name: homotopy links of strata / punctured tubular neighbourhoods; stratified fundamental groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn; MacPherson; Treumann; Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); Woolf

missed.claim: This is a worked toy example of Grothendieck's (Esquisse §5) programme: describe the homotopy type of a stratified moduli space by a diagram of punctured tubular neighbourhoods indexed by pairs or flags of strata. The 3×3 'product of spans' shape is the exit-path / link-poset diagram for a normal-crossing point. Since exit-path categories and homotopy links are now well established, this is only documentary evidence of how early and how concretely he worked it out, not a new result.
missed.quote: C×C comme somme amalgamée du diagramme suivant (de type produit de ←·→ par lui-même)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical documentation of Grothendieck's pre-1984 anticipation of exit-path / homotopy-link descriptions applied to the boundary of M_{g,n}. Mathematically routine today.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but elementary homotopy-pushout decompositions of C^2∖{0} and C^2 in a normal-crossing local model. Interest is only as a concrete illustration of the stratified-reconstruction programme later formalised by others.
transcription_corrections: The struck-out first attempt at the 3×3 diagram contains entries like D*×D* and D*×D* repeated, plus a crossed-out downward arrow to D*×D*. It is entirely cancelled.
Bottom-middle label: under D*×D there is '||' and V^{Δ1}_{P,x}. This is shown in the image with a vertical equality sign beneath the entry, not as a separate line.
Right margin: 'Somme amalgamée = C^2', set off by a vertical double bar.
In (280), the parenthesised line shows long arrows from C*×D and from D×C* converging to U = C^2∖{P}. The 'P' is written as a blackboard-bold P (the origin).
